# Website context

Visitor-facing story and marketing copy must sound like Abhishek speaking as “I”, “me”, and “my”, not an outside narrator describing him.

Use `[Abhishek to provide: ...]` in source/content notes where his own wording or personal facts are missing. Do not write first-person claims on his behalf or render authoring prompts on the live site. `[Fill in]` remains for non-copy decisions and details. Do not guess.

- [Project](project.md): goals, audience, and confirmed facts.
- [Pages and content](pages-content.md): page structure and copy inputs.
- [Design and motion](design.md): visual direction and GSAP.
- [SEO](seo.md): discoverability requirements.
- [Integrations](integrations.md): Strava and external services.

Third person may be used for internal project notes and factual labels, but not for the portfolio's narrative voice.
